subject: Concurrency SLO vs. Uptime: fast-path packaging & crediting questions
messages:
From: Tom Redding <tom.redding@atlasops.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Concurrency-based SLA & fast-path packaging questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our procurement and infra teams around how Redwood thinks about SLA credits when the key metric is concurrency rather than classic uptime percentage. Specifically:

- Does Redwood support a concurrency SLO (e.g., 500 concurrent requests sustained averaged over 5 minutes) and can credits be tied to minute-level breaches rather than hourly availability?
- For the "fast-path" lane you mentioned (priority execution / pre-warmed KV cache), how is that packaged and priced? Is it a flat premium, a per-request surcharge, or a reserved capacity SKU?
- If we sign a 12-month committed spend, what depth of discount can we realistically expect on both the concurrency SLO and the fast-path add-on? Our infra lead is worried about cold-start penalties for KV-heavy workloads and wants an assurance path.

Can you send a short pricing sketch and an example credit matrix we can show legal/finance? Low churn here — prefer short bullets and a simple table.

Attaching our internal procurement checklist in case it's helpful.

Best,
Tom
Procurement / AtlasOps
[Attachment: atlasops-procurement-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Redding <tom.redding@atlasops.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Concurrency-based SLA & fast-path packaging questions

Tom — great questions, thanks. I pulled Laura (pricing) and Grace (solutions) into the thread so we can give a short, actionable response and a matrix you can circulate. High level first, then an attachment with the numbers.

1) Concurrency SLOs and credit model (short):
- We support both classic uptime (% availability) and a concurrency-based SLO. For concurrency SLOs we measure sustained concurrent requests using a 1-minute sampling window and report both 1-min and 5-min rolling averages. Credits are applied at the minute level and accumulated daily into a single credit payout on a monthly invoice.
- Credit slabs: minute-level breaches are bucketed into three bands (minor, moderate, severe) based on % of target concurrency exceeded and duration. Minor: 5-10% over target for <15 minutes -> 5% monthly credit cap; Moderate: 10-50% over for 15-120 minutes -> 15% cap; Severe: >50% over or sustained >2 hours -> 35% cap. (See attached matrix for exact thresholds and examples.)

2) Fast-path / pre-warmed lane packaging:
- Fast-path is offered as two flavors:
  a) Reserved Fast-path Slice — a capacity SKU (per GPU-slot equivalent) guaranteeing pre-warmed worker capacity, KV priming, and lower queueing thresholds. Billed monthly as a reserved unit. Ideal for steady, predictable bursts.
  b) On-demand Priority — per-request priority tokens, billed per 1k priority requests, which use remaining fast-path capacity after reserved slices. Good for variable, spiky priority traffic.
- Fast-path includes enhanced KV cache priming for pinned prefixes and a reduced cold-start SLA (measured in p95 latency).

3) Commit discounts and concessions:
- Standard commercial: 10% discount on platform usage for 12-month revenue commit.
- Concession for AtlasOps early-stage MLP: can offer up to 15% off platform usage + 10% off reserved fast-path slices with a 12-month commit >= $300k ARR, and a 30-day notice for scaling reserved slices.
- We can also include a one-time credit to cover initial KV priming costs (applied as invoice credit over first 2 months).

Attached is a concise matrix (redwood-concurrency-slo-matrix.xlsx) showing example breach scenarios, credit calc, and a sample invoice line-item for reserved fast-path slices and on-demand tokens.

Next steps: if this looks directionally right, Grace will run a short tech note on KV priming behavior with your infra team and we can draft a commercial term sheet for legal.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

From: Tom Redding <tom.redding@atlasops.com>

Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Concurrency-based SLA & fast-path packaging questions

Karthik / Laura / Grace — thanks for the quick matrix, that's very helpful. A few clarifying points from our side after reviewing:

- The minute-level crediting model is attractive, but our legal team prefers a simpler cap tied to monthly spend rather than percent-of-month caps by band. Can you show an equivalent table where credits are expressed as USD caps per month for breach bands?
- AtlasOps runs KV-heavy inference where prefix priming costs are material. The one-time KV priming credit is helpful — can we expand that to cover the first 4 weeks and have it amortized across the first 3 invoices?
- Regarding fast-path reserved slices, would Redwood be open to a stepped reserved capacity discount (e.g., 10% for first slice, 12.5% for 3-5 slices, 15% beyond that) if we commit to a minimum 12-month reserved quantity?

If you're able to accommodate the USD-capped credit table and the expanded priming credit, we can move to term-sheet drafting. I've attached a short internal note with the finance team's ask.

Tom
Tom Redding
Head of Procurement — AtlasOps
[Attachment: AO-pricing-requests.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Redding <tom.redding@atlasops.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Concurrency-based SLA & fast-path packaging questions

Tom — appreciate the detail. We can do the following concessions to keep this moving:

- USD-capped credit table: yes. We've converted the percent caps to equivalent monthly USD ceilings tied to committed ARR tiers in the attached updated matrix. For AO at the $300k+ commit level the cap maps to the following illustrative numbers: Minor breach -> $2k/month cap; Moderate -> $8k/month cap; Severe -> $25k/month cap. Exact numbers will be finalized in the commercial term sheet.

- KV priming credit: we can expand the one-time credit to cover 4 weeks and amortize it across the first 3 invoices (applied as a line-item on each invoice). We'll show the amortization schedule in the term sheet.

- Stepped reserved-slice discount: agreeable in principle. Proposed schedule: 10% for slice 1, 12.5% for slices 2-4, 15% for slice 5+. This requires a 12-month minimum reserved slice commitment and a quarterly reconciliation.

Next steps: Laura will produce an updated pricing appendix and USD-capped credit table. Grace will schedule a 30-minute technical call to validate KV priming behavior with your infra team (I put a tentative link in the HubSpot activity). If that all looks good, we can hand off to commercial to draft a short form term sheet and a DocuSign envelope.

I'll follow up with the updated appendix by EOD tomorrow. Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

-Karthik
